entry.title: I built a Resume Killer using Next.js, Neo4j, and Gemini
entry.summary:
The Problem: I was tired of ATS bots rejecting me. I knew I had the skills, but my resume didn't show it. The Idea: What if I could visualize my GitHub commit history as a dependency tree? The Stack: Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router) Database: Neo4j (Graph DB is perfect for skill trees) AI: Gemini (To analyse "Impact" vs "Churn" in code) How it works: It fetches your public repos. It maps languages to nodes (e.g., React -> Frontend). It calculates a "Market Readiness" score. Try it out: I just launched the MVP today. It's free for devs. I'd love to see if the graph accurately reflects your stack. 👉 https://www.skillnode.dev/
The "Magic" Query Here is the actual Cypher query I use in Neo4j to map the skill dependencies. It finds a user, matches their commits, and calculates the weight of the relationship:
MATCH (u:User {username: $username})-[r:COMMITTED]->(c:Commit) WHERE c.impact_score > 50 MATCH (c)-[:USES_LANGUAGE]->(l:Language) MERGE (u)-[s:HAS_SKILL]->(l) ON CREATE SET s.weight = 1 ON MATCH SET s.weight = s.weight + 1 RETURN u, s, l
(This is just a simplified version, but you get the idea—it weights skills based on actual usage, not just claiming you know them.)

entry.title: Digital Identity Verification for Banks & NBFCs
entry.summary: The "Digital Arrest Scam" of 2025-2026 highlights the urgent need for advanced digital identity verification in banking. Traditional KYC systems are now vulnerable to deepfakes and synthetic identities, enabling sophisticated fraud through "mule accounts." For banks and NBFCs, upgrading online KYC is crucial for survival, not just compliance, without compromising customer experience. Effective digital verification relies on multi-layered security. For account opening, this includes forensic document scans checking for pixel tampering, real-time database validation of PAN and Aadhaar, and AI-powered Video KYC. Critically, "Passive Liveness Detection" verifies the presence of a living human by analyzing micro-reflections and blood flow, a capability deepfakes currently lack. Geo-location checks during video calls also flag suspicious access points. In lending, combating synthetic identities requires "bank account verification" (penny drop). A nominal deposit confirms the legal name associated with the account, preventing funds from reaching third-party mule accounts. The RBI maintains a strict stance, holding banks liable for lax KYC leading to mule account operations. The future involves "Continuous Behavioral Verification," moving beyond single-point identity checks to ongoing authentication based on user patterns. Integrating modular APIs for these advanced capabilities allows financial institutions to fortify their systems against evolving threats, protecting both their balance sheets and vulnerable customers.
